questions.question: Which command displays the current systemd target?
questions.explanation: systemctl get-default shows the current systemd target (e.g., graphical.target, multi-user.target).
questions.hint8020: systemctl get-default = current target. systemctl set-default = change it. Targets replace runlevels in systemd.

questions.question: Which file stores the system's static hostname in systemd-based distributions?
questions.explanation: /etc/hostname stores the static hostname in systemd distributions. hostnamectl reads and writes this file.
questions.hint8020: /etc/hostname = static hostname. hostnamectl set-hostname = change it. /etc/hosts maps hostnames to IPs locally.

questions.question: Which command creates a new LVM logical volume named 'data' of 10GB in volume group 'vg0'?
questions.explanation: lvcreate -L 10G sets size, -n data names it, vg0 is the volume group.
questions.hint8020: LVM flow: pvcreate → vgcreate → lvcreate. -L = size, -n = name, last arg = VG. lvextend to grow, lvreduce to shrink.

questions.question: Which command resizes an ext4 filesystem after extending its logical volume?
questions.explanation: resize2fs resizes ext2/3/4 filesystems. For online resizing, use resize2fs on a mounted filesystem.
questions.hint8020: resize2fs = ext2/3/4. xfs_growfs = XFS (only grow, can't shrink). Always lvextend first, then resize filesystem.

questions.question: Where is the EFI system partition typically mounted?
questions.explanation: The EFI System Partition (ESP) is typically mounted at /boot/efi in Linux systems.
questions.hint8020: ESP = /boot/efi, FAT32 formatted. Contains bootloaders. BIOS uses MBR, UEFI uses GPT + ESP.

questions.question: Which command shows the UUID of all block devices?
questions.explanation: blkid shows UUIDs, filesystem types, and labels. lsblk -o UUID also shows UUIDs for block devices.
questions.hint8020: blkid = quick UUID lookup. Use UUIDs in /etc/fstab instead of device names — they survive disk reordering.

questions.question: Which GRUB2 configuration file should be edited to make persistent boot changes?
questions.explanation: /etc/default/grub is the configuration file. After editing, run grub2-mkconfig to regenerate grub.cfg.
questions.hint8020: Edit /etc/default/grub → run grub2-mkconfig (RHEL) or update-grub (Debian). Never edit grub.cfg directly.

questions.question: Which command regenerates the GRUB2 configuration after editing /etc/default/grub?
questions.explanation: grub2-mkconfig (RHEL) and update-grub (Debian) both regenerate the GRUB configuration.
questions.hint8020: RHEL = grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg. Debian = update-grub (wrapper script). Same result, different distro.

questions.question: Which command loads a kernel module manually?
questions.explanation: modprobe loads modules with dependency resolution. insmod loads a single module file without dependencies.
questions.hint8020: modprobe = smart (resolves deps). insmod = manual (no deps). modinfo = show module info. lsmod = list loaded modules.

questions.question: Which file defines kernel parameters to set at boot via sysctl?
questions.explanation: /etc/sysctl.conf and files in /etc/sysctl.d/ define kernel parameters loaded at boot. Apply with sysctl -p.
questions.hint8020: /etc/sysctl.conf = persistent kernel params. sysctl -p = reload. sysctl -w key=value = set temporarily. /proc/sys = live values.

questions.question: Which command displays the current network configuration using the iproute2 toolset?
questions.explanation: ip addr show (or ip a) displays all network interfaces and their addresses. Part of the modern iproute2 suite.
questions.hint8020: ip a = addresses. ip r = routes. ip l = links. ip n = neighbors (ARP). iproute2 replaces ifconfig/route/arp.

questions.question: Which command displays the partition table of a disk using GPT format?
questions.explanation: gdisk is GPT-native, fdisk and parted can both read GPT partition tables. gdisk is preferred for GPT operations.
questions.hint8020: gdisk = GPT disks. fdisk = MBR (also reads GPT). parted = both MBR + GPT. sgdisk = scripting-friendly GPT tool.

questions.question: Which command sets SELinux to permissive mode?
questions.explanation: setenforce 0 sets SELinux to permissive (1=enforcing). sestatus only shows the current status.
questions.hint8020: setenforce 0 = permissive (logs only). setenforce 1 = enforcing (blocks). /etc/selinux/config = persistent mode.

questions.question: Which file contains the SELinux configuration for the permanent mode?
questions.explanation: /etc/selinux/config is the main config. /etc/sysconfig/selinux is often a symlink to it on RHEL.
questions.hint8020: /etc/selinux/config sets SELINUX=enforcing|permissive|disabled. Requires reboot to switch to/from disabled.

questions.question: Which command generates SSH key pairs?
questions.explanation: ssh-keygen generates SSH public/private key pairs. Default location: ~/.ssh/id_rsa or id_ed25519.
questions.hint8020: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 = modern, fast. ssh-copy-id = deploy public key. ~/.ssh/authorized_keys = server-side public keys.

questions.question: Which command displays the status of AppArmor for all profiles?
questions.explanation: aa-status shows the status of all AppArmor profiles (enforce, complain, or disabled).
questions.hint8020: AppArmor: aa-status = check, aa-enforce = enforce, aa-complain = log only. Profiles in /etc/apparmor.d/. Ubuntu default MAC.

questions.question: Which nftables table family is used for IPv4 traffic?
questions.explanation: The 'ip' family in nftables handles IPv4. 'inet' handles both IPv4 and IPv6.
questions.hint8020: nftables families: ip (v4), ip6 (v6), inet (both), arp, bridge. nft = command. Replaces iptables/ip6tables.

questions.question: Which PAM module is used for password complexity requirements?
questions.explanation: pam_pwquality (successor to pam_cracklib) enforces password quality requirements in PAM.
questions.hint8020: pam_pwquality = password rules (minlen, dcredit, ucredit). Config: /etc/security/pwquality.conf. PAM stack in /etc/pam.d/.

questions.question: Which command shows the SELinux context of files?
questions.explanation: ls -Z shows SELinux security contexts. -Z is the context flag for ls, ps, and other tools.
questions.hint8020: ls -Z = file contexts. ps -Z = process contexts. chcon = change context temporarily. restorecon = restore default context.

questions.question: Where are the sudo privilege rules defined?
questions.explanation: /etc/sudoers contains sudo rules. Edit with visudo to ensure syntax checking.
questions.hint8020: /etc/sudoers = rules. ALWAYS use visudo to edit (syntax check). Drop-in files in /etc/sudoers.d/ for per-user rules.

questions.question: Which command encrypts a block device using LUKS?
questions.explanation: cryptsetup luksFormat initializes LUKS encryption on a partition. cryptsetup luksOpen to unlock.
questions.hint8020: LUKS flow: luksFormat → luksOpen → mkfs → mount. luksClose to lock. /etc/crypttab for boot-time unlock.

questions.question: Which command adds a firewall rule using ufw to allow SSH?
questions.explanation: ufw allow ssh permits SSH traffic (port 22). ufw is the Uncomplicated Firewall frontend for iptables/nftables.
questions.hint8020: ufw allow ssh = port 22. ufw enable = activate. ufw status verbose = show rules. ufw deny = block. Simple frontend for nftables.

questions.question: Which command reloads a systemd service configuration without restarting?
questions.explanation: systemctl reload reloads configuration. restart stops and starts the service.
questions.hint8020: reload = re-read config (no downtime). restart = stop + start. reload-or-restart = try reload, fall back to restart.

questions.question: Which file configures the DNS resolver in modern systemd-based systems?
questions.explanation: systemd-resolved manages DNS via /etc/systemd/resolved.conf. /etc/resolv.conf may be a symlink.
questions.hint8020: /etc/systemd/resolved.conf = systemd DNS. /etc/resolv.conf often symlinked to resolved. resolvectl status = check DNS.

questions.question: Which command shows listening TCP ports with process information?
questions.explanation: ss (modern), netstat (traditional), and lsof can all show listening ports with process info.
questions.hint8020: ss -tlnp = fastest. t=TCP, l=listening, n=numeric, p=process. ss replaces netstat. lsof -i = by protocol.

questions.question: Which Apache configuration directive defines the document root?
questions.explanation: DocumentRoot in Apache defines the directory from which web content is served.
questions.hint8020: DocumentRoot = web files. ServerRoot = Apache install. Listen = port. VirtualHost = multi-site. apachectl -t = test config.

questions.question: Which directive schedules weekly execution in a systemd timer unit?
questions.explanation: OnCalendar=weekly in a .timer unit schedules weekly execution. systemd timers replace cron.
questions.hint8020: OnCalendar= in .timer files. daily, weekly, monthly, or specific: *-*-* 03:00:00. systemctl list-timers = show active timers.

questions.question: Which directive in nginx.conf defines the server name?
questions.explanation: server_name in nginx defines the hostname for a virtual server.
questions.hint8020: nginx: server_name = hostname. listen = port. root = document root. location = URL routing. nginx -t = test config.

questions.question: Which command shows the current mail queue in Postfix?
questions.explanation: mailq and postqueue -p both display the Postfix mail queue.
questions.hint8020: mailq = show queue. postqueue -f = flush queue. postfix reload = reload config. /etc/postfix/main.cf = main config.

questions.question: Which DHCP server configuration file is used on Debian/Ubuntu?
questions.explanation: /etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf is the ISC DHCP server configuration file on Debian/Ubuntu systems.
questions.hint8020: /etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf = DHCP server config. Defines subnets, ranges, options. dhclient = client. /var/lib/dhcp/dhcpd.leases = lease db.

questions.question: Which command configures network connections using NetworkManager CLI?
questions.explanation: nmcli is the NetworkManager command-line interface for managing connections, devices, and profiles.
questions.hint8020: nmcli con show = list connections. nmcli dev status = device status. nmcli con add = create. nmtui = text UI alternative.

questions.question: Which protocol does SSSD use to authenticate users against Active Directory?
questions.explanation: SSSD uses LDAP for user/group lookup and Kerberos for authentication when joining Active Directory.
questions.hint8020: SSSD = System Security Services Daemon. AD join: realm join. Uses LDAP (directory) + Kerberos (auth). Config: /etc/sssd/sssd.conf.

questions.question: Which Ansible module is used to install packages across distributions?
questions.explanation: The 'package' module is the generic module that works across distributions (apt, yum, dnf).
questions.hint8020: package = distro-agnostic. apt = Debian only. yum/dnf = RHEL only. Use 'package' in playbooks for portability.

questions.question: Which Ansible command runs a playbook?
questions.explanation: ansible-playbook executes Ansible playbooks. ansible runs ad-hoc commands.
questions.hint8020: ansible-playbook = run playbook. ansible = ad-hoc command. ansible-galaxy = roles/collections. ansible-vault = encrypt secrets.

questions.question: Which command traces system calls made by a process?
questions.explanation: strace traces system calls. ltrace traces library calls. Both are essential debugging tools.
questions.hint8020: strace = system calls (open, read, write, fork). ltrace = library calls (printf, malloc). strace -p PID = attach to running process.

questions.question: Which bash construct tests if a file exists and is a regular file?
questions.explanation: -f tests for regular file. -e tests existence (any type). -d tests for directory. -r tests if readable.
questions.hint8020: Test flags: -f = regular file, -d = directory, -e = exists, -r = readable, -w = writable, -x = executable, -s = non-empty.

questions.question: Which tool creates a systemd service from a script for automatic startup?
questions.explanation: Custom systemd services are defined by creating .service unit files in /etc/systemd/system/. Then enable with systemctl enable.
questions.hint8020: Create /etc/systemd/system/myservice.service with [Unit], [Service], [Install] sections. systemctl daemon-reload after creating.

questions.question: Which command schedules a one-time task to run at 3 AM tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The 'at' command schedules one-time tasks. atq lists pending jobs. atrm removes them.
questions.hint8020: at = one-time jobs. cron = recurring. at 3am tomorrow, at now + 2 hours. atq = list queue. atrm = remove job.

questions.question: Which shebang line specifies a Python 3 script?
questions.explanation: #!/usr/bin/env python3 uses env to find python3 in PATH, making scripts portable across installations.
questions.hint8020: #!/usr/bin/env python3 = portable. #!/usr/bin/python3 = fixed path. env searches PATH. Always use env for portability.

questions.question: Which Git command creates a new branch and switches to it?
questions.explanation: git checkout -b creates a new branch and switches to it. git switch -c is the modern equivalent.
questions.hint8020: git checkout -b = create + switch. git switch -c = modern equivalent. git branch = just create. git merge = integrate changes.

questions.question: Which command shows the last 20 system boot messages?
questions.explanation: dmesg shows kernel ring buffer messages. journalctl --boot shows boot logs from the current boot.
questions.hint8020: dmesg = kernel messages. journalctl -b = current boot, -b -1 = previous boot. journalctl -p err = errors only.

questions.question: Which command shows network interface statistics and errors?
questions.explanation: ip -s link, ifconfig, and ethtool can all display interface statistics and error counters.
questions.hint8020: ip -s link = traffic stats. ethtool -S = detailed NIC stats. ethtool eth0 = speed/duplex. Watch for TX/RX errors.

questions.question: Which command shows the routing table?
questions.explanation: ip route (modern), route -n (traditional), and netstat -r all display the routing table.
questions.hint8020: ip route = modern. Default route = gateway. ip route add = add route. ip route del = remove. 'via' = next hop.

questions.question: Which file contains the kernel messages log?
questions.explanation: Kernel messages go to /var/log/kern.log, /var/log/messages (RHEL), or /var/log/syslog (Debian).
questions.hint8020: Debian: kern.log + syslog. RHEL: messages. Both use rsyslog or journald. journalctl -k = kernel messages from journal.

questions.question: Which command shows the I/O statistics per block device?
questions.explanation: iostat shows I/O statistics, iotop shows per-process I/O, blktrace traces block I/O operations.
questions.hint8020: iostat = device-level I/O. iotop = process-level I/O (like top for disk). Part of sysstat package. iostat -x = extended stats.

questions.question: Which command monitors system resource usage in real time, showing CPU, memory, and process details?
questions.explanation: top (built-in), htop (interactive), and vmstat (snapshot) all monitor system resources in different ways.
questions.hint8020: top = built-in, press 1 for per-CPU. htop = interactive (F5 tree view). vmstat 1 = 1s intervals. uptime = quick load check.

questions.question: Which command checks filesystem integrity on an unmounted ext4 partition?
questions.explanation: fsck is the generic frontend that calls e2fsck for ext filesystems. Both work on ext2/3/4. Partition must be unmounted.
questions.hint8020: fsck = generic. e2fsck = ext2/3/4. xfs_repair = XFS. NEVER run on mounted filesystem. Boot to rescue mode if root partition.

questions.question: A system fails to boot and drops to an emergency shell. Which command checks for filesystem errors on the root partition?
questions.explanation: fsck -y automatically fixes errors. In emergency mode the root filesystem is read-only, so fsck can safely run.
questions.hint8020: Emergency shell: root is read-only. fsck -y = auto-fix. After fix: reboot. If GRUB broken: boot from live USB, chroot, grub-install.

questions.question: Which command shows disk space usage with human-readable sizes?
questions.explanation: df -h shows filesystem disk space usage in human-readable format (KB, MB, GB).
questions.hint8020: df -h = filesystem usage (free space). du -sh = directory size. df -i = inode usage. 100% inodes = can't create files even with space.

questions.question: Which tool captures and analyzes network packets on a Linux system?
questions.explanation: tcpdump (CLI), wireshark (GUI), and tshark (CLI wireshark) all capture and analyze network packets.
questions.hint8020: tcpdump -i eth0 = capture on interface. -w file.pcap = save. wireshark = GUI analysis. tshark = CLI wireshark. Use BPF filters.

questions.question: Which command lists all physical volumes in LVM?
questions.explanation: pvs (summary), pvdisplay (detailed), and pvscan (scan for new PVs) all list physical volumes.
questions.hint8020: pvs = quick list. pvdisplay = detailed. vgs/vgdisplay = volume groups. lvs/lvdisplay = logical volumes. LVM hierarchy: PV → VG → LV.

questions.question: Which command creates a RAID 5 array using mdadm?
questions.explanation: mdadm --create builds a new array. --level=5 sets RAID 5. --raid-devices specifies the number of disks.
questions.hint8020: mdadm --create = new array. --level= 0(stripe), 1(mirror), 5(parity), 6(double parity), 10(stripe+mirror). /proc/mdstat = status.

questions.question: Which file is used to configure automatic mounting of filesystems at boot?
questions.explanation: /etc/fstab contains filesystem mount entries that are applied at boot. /etc/mtab and /proc/mounts show currently mounted filesystems.
questions.hint8020: /etc/fstab columns: device, mountpoint, type, options, dump, fsck-order. Use UUID= for device identification. nofail = don't block boot.

questions.question: Which command installs packages from a .deb file including dependencies?
questions.explanation: apt install ./package.deb installs the local .deb file and resolves dependencies. dpkg -i installs but does not resolve dependencies.
questions.hint8020: apt install ./file.deb = install + deps. dpkg -i = install only (no deps). dpkg -l = list installed. apt-get -f install = fix broken deps.

questions.question: Which command manages DNF repository configuration on RHEL-based systems?
questions.explanation: dnf config-manager (modern) and yum-config-manager (legacy) both manage repository configuration on RHEL.
questions.hint8020: dnf config-manager --add-repo URL = add repo. --enable/--disable repo_id. /etc/yum.repos.d/ = repo config files. dnf repolist = show repos.

questions.question: Which systemd unit type starts a service at a specific time or interval?
questions.explanation: A .timer unit triggers a corresponding .service unit at specified times or intervals, replacing cron for systemd.
questions.hint8020: .timer = schedule. .service = what to run. OnCalendar= for time-based. OnBootSec= for delay after boot. systemctl list-timers.

questions.question: Which command shows detailed hardware information on a Linux system?
questions.explanation: lshw, dmidecode (SMBIOS/DMI), and hwinfo all display detailed hardware information in different formats.
questions.hint8020: lshw = full hardware tree. dmidecode = BIOS/firmware data. lscpu = CPU. lspci = PCI. lsusb = USB. lsblk = block devices.

questions.question: Which command creates a swap file and enables it?
questions.explanation: Create with dd or fallocate, format with mkswap, activate with swapon. Add to /etc/fstab for persistence.
questions.hint8020: dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile bs=1M count=1024 → mkswap /swapfile → swapon /swapfile. chmod 600. Add to /etc/fstab with swap type.

questions.question: Which command shows the current kernel version?
questions.explanation: uname -r shows just the kernel release. /proc/version shows the full kernel version string including build information.
questions.hint8020: uname -r = release. uname -a = all info. /proc/version = detailed build info. uname -m = architecture (x86_64, aarch64).

questions.question: Which command restores the default SELinux context on a file?
questions.explanation: restorecon restores SELinux contexts based on the policy. -R for recursive, -v for verbose.
questions.hint8020: restorecon = reset to policy default. chcon = temporary change (lost on relabel). semanage fcontext = permanent custom context.

questions.question: Which command displays failed login attempts on a Linux system?
questions.explanation: lastb reads /var/log/btmp for bad logins, faillog shows failure counts, and journalctl can filter SSH failures.
questions.hint8020: lastb = failed logins (/var/log/btmp). last = successful logins (/var/log/wtmp). faillog = failure counts. lastlog = last login per user.

questions.question: Which file defines which users can log in to the system?
questions.explanation: /etc/security/access.conf is used by pam_access to control login access. /etc/securetty restricts root login terminals.
questions.hint8020: access.conf = pam_access rules (+ allow, - deny). /etc/nologin = block non-root logins. /etc/securetty = root-only terminal list.

questions.question: Which command scans for rootkits on a Linux system?
questions.explanation: rkhunter and chkrootkit scan for rootkits. lynis performs a comprehensive security audit including rootkit detection.
questions.hint8020: rkhunter = rootkit scanner. chkrootkit = alternative scanner. lynis = full audit. aide/tripwire = file integrity monitoring.

questions.question: Which command configures an nftables rule to drop incoming traffic on port 23?
options: nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 23 drop
Both nft add rule and iptables commands
questions.explanation: nft is the native nftables command. iptables commands are still supported via the iptables-nft translation layer.
questions.hint8020: nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 23 drop. inet = IPv4+IPv6. iptables-nft = compatibility layer. nft list ruleset = show all rules.

questions.question: Which command sets file capabilities to allow a binary to bind to privileged ports without root?
questions.explanation: setcap grants specific Linux capabilities. cap_net_bind_service allows binding to ports below 1024 without root.
questions.hint8020: setcap = fine-grained privileges. getcap = check caps. Replaces SUID for specific privileges. Capabilities: net_bind, raw, admin, sys_ptrace.

questions.question: Which command creates a new user with a home directory and specific shell?
questions.explanation: useradd -m creates the home directory, -s sets the login shell. adduser is a higher-level wrapper on Debian.
questions.hint8020: useradd -m = create home. -s = shell. -G = supplementary groups. -d = custom home path. usermod = modify existing. userdel -r = delete + home.

questions.question: Which NFS configuration file defines exported directories?
questions.explanation: /etc/exports defines directories shared via NFS. exportfs -ra reloads the configuration.
questions.hint8020: /etc/exports: /shared 192.168.1.0/24(rw,sync,no_root_squash). exportfs -ra = reload. showmount -e = list exports. Client: mount -t nfs.

questions.question: Which command configures a Samba share on Linux?
questions.explanation: /etc/samba/smb.conf is the Samba configuration file. testparm validates the configuration syntax.
questions.hint8020: /etc/samba/smb.conf = config. testparm = validate. smbpasswd -a user = add Samba user. smbclient = connect to shares. pdbedit = manage users.

questions.question: Which command manages user passwords including expiration and aging?
questions.explanation: chage sets password aging policies: -M max days, -m min days, -W warning days, -I inactive days, -E expire date.
questions.hint8020: chage -l user = show aging. chage -M 90 = max 90 days. chage -E 2025-12-31 = account expires. /etc/login.defs = system defaults.

questions.question: Which command sets up a BIND DNS zone file?
options: Edit /etc/named.conf and create zone file in /var/named/
questions.explanation: BIND DNS configuration requires editing /etc/named.conf to define zones and creating zone files in /var/named/.
questions.hint8020: /etc/named.conf = main config. /var/named/ = zone files. named-checkconf = verify config. named-checkzone = verify zone file. rndc reload.

questions.question: Which command creates a new group and adds an existing user to it?
questions.explanation: groupadd creates the group. usermod -aG appends the user to the supplementary group without removing existing groups.
questions.hint8020: groupadd = create. usermod -aG = append to group (-a is critical, without it replaces all groups). id user = verify groups. newgrp = switch active group.

questions.question: Which command configures a static IP address using NetworkManager?
options: nmcli con mod 'connection' ipv4.addresses 192.168.1.10/24 ipv4.method manual
questions.explanation: nmcli con mod sets persistent connection properties. ifconfig and ip addr add are temporary (lost on reboot).
questions.hint8020: nmcli con mod = persistent config. ipv4.method manual = static. ipv4.gateway = gateway. nmcli con up = apply. ip addr add = temporary.

questions.question: Which file controls the Name Service Switch for user authentication sources?
questions.explanation: /etc/nsswitch.conf determines the order of name service sources: files, ldap, sss, nis for users, groups, hosts, etc.
questions.hint8020: /etc/nsswitch.conf: passwd: files sss ldap. hosts: files dns. Determines lookup order. getent = query NSS databases.

questions.question: Which bash variable holds the exit status of the last command?
questions.explanation: $? contains the exit status of the last executed command. 0 means success, non-zero means failure.
questions.hint8020: $? = exit status (0=success). $! = last background PID. $# = arg count. $0 = script name. $@ = all args. $$ = current PID.

questions.question: Which command finds all files larger than 100MB in the /home directory?
questions.explanation: find -size +100M finds files larger than 100 megabytes. + means greater than, - means less than.
questions.hint8020: find -size +100M = over 100MB. -type f = files only. -mtime -7 = modified in 7 days. -exec rm {} \; = delete found files. -name '*.log' = by name.

questions.question: Which cron expression runs a job every weekday at 6:30 AM?
questions.explanation: Cron format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. 30 6 = 6:30 AM. 1-5 = Monday through Friday.
questions.hint8020: Cron: min hour dom month dow. 0=Sunday or 7=Sunday. 1-5 = Mon-Fri. */5 = every 5. crontab -e = edit. crontab -l = list.

questions.question: Which command extracts specific columns from a CSV file?
questions.explanation: cut -d',' -f1,3 extracts columns 1 and 3 using comma delimiter. awk -F',' does the same with more flexibility.
questions.hint8020: cut -d = delimiter, -f = fields. awk -F = field separator, $1 = first field. cut = simple extraction. awk = powerful processing.

questions.question: Which Ansible inventory file format is used by default?
questions.explanation: Ansible supports both INI and YAML inventory formats. The default location is /etc/ansible/hosts.
questions.hint8020: INI: [webservers] + host lines. YAML: all: hosts: children:. -i = custom inventory. Dynamic inventory = script/plugin that generates host list.

questions.question: Which command compiles and runs a container image using a Dockerfile?
options: docker build -t myimage . && docker run myimage
questions.explanation: docker build -t tags the image, . is the build context. docker run creates and starts a container from the image.
questions.hint8020: docker build -t name:tag . = build image. docker run -d -p 80:80 = detached + port map. Dockerfile: FROM, RUN, COPY, CMD, EXPOSE.

questions.question: Which command redirects both stdout and stderr to a file?
questions.explanation: &> redirects both streams (bash shortcut). > file 2>&1 redirects stdout to file, then stderr to stdout's destination.
questions.hint8020: 1 = stdout, 2 = stderr. > = redirect stdout. 2>&1 = stderr to stdout. &> = both. /dev/null = discard. | = pipe stdout only. |& = pipe both.

questions.question: A user reports they cannot create new files despite having disk space available. Which command diagnoses this?
questions.explanation: df -i shows inode usage. If inodes are exhausted (100%), no new files can be created even with free disk space.
questions.hint8020: df -i = inode usage. Inodes exhausted = no new files. Many small files consume inodes. find / -xdev -type f | wc -l = count files.

questions.question: Which command identifies which process is using a specific file or port?
questions.explanation: lsof lists open files/ports by process. fuser identifies processes using files/mounts. ss shows socket/port usage.
questions.hint8020: lsof /path = who has file open. lsof -i :80 = who uses port 80. fuser -m /mount = processes on mount. fuser -k = kill those processes.

questions.question: Which command displays memory usage including buffers and cache?
questions.explanation: free -h shows memory with human-readable sizes. vmstat shows virtual memory stats. /proc/meminfo has detailed breakdowns.
questions.hint8020: free -h: total, used, free, shared, buff/cache, available. 'available' = truly free memory. Linux uses spare RAM for cache = normal.

questions.question: A service fails to start. Which command shows the most recent log entries for that service?
questions.explanation: journalctl -u filters by unit. systemctl status shows recent log lines. Both help diagnose service failures.
questions.hint8020: journalctl -u service = unit logs. -xe = end + explanations. --since '1 hour ago'. systemctl status = quick check with last few lines.

questions.question: Which command tests DNS resolution from the command line?
questions.explanation: dig (detailed), nslookup (interactive), and host (simple) all perform DNS lookups.
questions.hint8020: dig = most detailed (ANSWER section). nslookup = interactive mode. host = simplest. dig +short = just the answer. dig @8.8.8.8 = specific server.

questions.question: Which command traces the network path to a remote host?
questions.explanation: traceroute, tracepath, and mtr all show the network path. mtr combines traceroute and ping for continuous monitoring.
questions.hint8020: traceroute = show hops. tracepath = no root needed. mtr = continuous traceroute + ping stats. * = hop doesn't respond (firewall).

questions.question: A system is running slowly. Which command shows per-process CPU and memory usage sorted by CPU?
questions.explanation: ps aux --sort sorts by CPU percentage. top -o sorts columns. htop allows interactive sorting with F6.
questions.hint8020: ps aux --sort=-%cpu = top CPU consumers. top: press P (CPU sort), M (memory sort). load average > CPU count = overloaded.

questions.question: Which command checks if a remote port is open and accepting connections?
questions.explanation: nc (netcat) with -z scans ports. nmap scans with more detail. telnet tests TCP connectivity.
questions.hint8020: nc -zv host 80 = quick port check. nmap -p 22,80,443 = scan specific ports. ss -tlnp on server side = verify listening.

questions.question: Which log file records authentication events on RHEL-based systems?
questions.explanation: /var/log/secure on RHEL records authentication events. Debian uses /var/log/auth.log for the same purpose.
questions.hint8020: RHEL: /var/log/secure. Debian: /var/log/auth.log. Both log SSH, sudo, PAM events. auditd logs go to /var/log/audit/audit.log.

questions.question: Which command kills a process that is not responding to SIGTERM?
questions.explanation: kill -9 (SIGKILL) forcefully terminates a process that ignores SIGTERM (signal 15). Cannot be caught or ignored.
questions.hint8020: SIGTERM (15) = graceful stop (can be caught). SIGKILL (9) = force kill (cannot be caught). Always try SIGTERM first. killall = by name.
